title: Thonny Window Tour
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: A clickable mockup of the Thonny IDE with numbered hotspots for the interpreter selector, editor, Run and Stop buttons, Shell, and the two Files panes, plus a quiz mode.

learningObjectives: Identify the editor, Shell, Run button, Stop button, interpreter selector and Files panes in Thonny
Explain what each part of the Thonny window is used for
Distinguish files stored on "This computer" from files stored on the MicroPython device
prerequisites: Thonny installed on the computer (see Desktop Setup)
A Raspberry Pi Pico connected with a data USB cable

accessibility.notes: Controls are standard HTML form elements; the canvas has a describe() text for screen readers

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Labeled diagram exploration followed by a click-to-answer quiz
keyQuestions: Where do you type a single test line?
How do you get the >>> prompt back from a runaway loop?
Which files run when the Pico is unplugged from the computer?
commonMisconceptions: A program saved on the laptop will run on the Pico by itself
The Shell and the editor do the same job
Closing Thonny stops a main.py that is already running on the Pico
assessmentOpportunities: Students answer all seven quiz questions correctly.
Students explain the difference between saving to "This computer" and to the MicroPython device.
Students can stop a running program from Thonny without unplugging the Pico.
